title: Painted World of Ariandel
snippet:
Painted World of Ariandel -  Dark Souls III - location - lead 
 lead : The **Painted World of Ariandel** is a location in *Dark Souls III*, accessible through the downloadable content *Ashes of Ariandel*.

title: Sister Friede
snippet: Over time Friede earned the trust of some painting inhabitants, to the point that the Corvian Knights of their village became infatuated with her. Above all, she managed to get close to Father Ariandel, a great Corvian who guarded the Flame inside the Painted World. His task was to unleash the Flame when the painting stagnated and began to rot, a custom intended for making way for the next painted world. However, when the painting began to be corrupted and its inhabitants made up their minds to burn it away, Friede opposed their wish, preferring a slow death in the comforting rot to the renewing change of the Flame. She convinced Ariandel to bury the Flame of the painting and to quench it with his blood, while her Corvian Knights swore to "protect" the painting from fire, even killing their brethren who opposed Friede. The Painter was imprisoned in the library of the corvian village and guarded by Sir Vilhelm, to prevent her from restoring the painting. His Lady's imprisonment

title: Father Ariandel
snippet:
Father Ariandel -  Dark Souls III - boss - lore 
 lore : Father Ariandel is the keeper of the Painted World of Ariandel, thought to have been the most recent one to restore it after the Painted World of Ariamis rotted away. When he met the Unkindled Sister Elfriede, she convinced him to forgo the destruction of his rotting world, and to stifle the flame that would burn it to be replaced by a new world by the next restorer, choosing to rot together

He constantly flails himself, bleeding onto the flame, to prevent the fire from burning his world, for he used blood in the restoration, and only that blood could prevent the fire from blazing again. When Friede's blood flows to the bowl containing the flame, the sight of her corpse enrages Father Ariandel, causing him to break free and strike the bowl against her unkindled blood to spark the flame and revive her by restoring her ember as an unkindled.

title: Painted World of Ariandel
snippet:
Painted World of Ariandel -  Dark Souls III - location - description 
 description : When the Ashen One reaches the Painted World, they will discover that this land is strange, cold and snow coated, and filled with deadly enemies, just like the Lordran's Painted World of Ariamis.

There are some differences with Ariamis, though; first of all, the area is larger and also there are many new enemies. The player will recognize some similar structures anyway, such as the wooden bridge that leads to a cathedral. There is also a tower reminiscent of Priscilla's tower.

She came to accept the Painted World as her new home; she also discovered that she wished to "protect" its forlorn inhabitants. Over time Friede earned their trust, to the point that the Corvian Knights who protected the village became infatuated with her; above all, she managed to get close to Father Ariandel, a Great Corvian who had the task of guarding the Flame within the Painted World and to burn it when the painting began to rot. This was done to bring the Painting back to life, thus avoiding the fate of the stagnant outside world, and make way for a new Painted World. title: Sister Friede
snippet: Friede remained in the chapel of the Painted World, guarding the Flame and Father Ariandel against trespassers, while the inhabitants of the painting rotted and filthy insects spread. When an Ashen One arrived in the painting, she would kindly but firmly invite them to leave and return to the outside world, leaving the inhabitants of the painting in peace and forgetting about them. When they ignored her advice and descended the chapel to confront Father Ariandel, she would be forced to wield her scythe and confront them, not before asking Father Ariandel to turn his gaze away from the imminent carnage. When she is defeated the first time, an enraged Ariandel sparks the Flame he bled so much to subdue, in a desperate attempt to revive her. Now rekindled, Friede would come back from death to fight by his side, their souls linked. After falling a second time, Friede would rise yet again thanks to her inner Dark Flame, in a final struggle to defeat the Ashen One and prevent the Painted

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - the_painted_world_of_ariandel 
 the_painted_world_of_ariandel : Within the Cathedral of the Deep the Ashen One can encounter Slave Knight Gael, a Slave Knight who seeks unkindled ash to aid his Lady. Gael presents the Ashen One with a fragment of the Painted World of Ariandel, which sucks the Ashen One in. Within the painting, the Ashen One encounters Sister Friede and her loyal knight Sir Vilhelm. Friede is an advisor to Ariandel, the painting's creator, and convinced him to allow the painting to rot rather than allow it to be destroyed and replaced by a new one, despite the wishes of many of the painting's denizens. Friede bids the Ashen One to leave, telling them that they do not belong in the Painted World.

 general_information : The Peculiar Doll is used to enter the Painted World of Ariamis. To enter the Painted World, players need to have the Peculiar Doll in their inventory and examine the large painting in the cathedral in Anor Londo.

The Peculiar doll is lost at the end of each playthrough and must be collected again in order to access the Painted World in NG+.

title: Slave Knight Gael
snippet: Nevertheless, the tales of the painting also told of a prophecy: "When the Ashes are two, a flame alighteth". If another Ash were to enter the Painting, there would yet be hope to kindle the flame and burn the rotten world away. And so Gael fled the Painted World, taking with him a rotten scrap of it, to seek out another Unkindled who could show Flame to his Lady. After a long, unsuccessful search, Gael would find himself in the Cleansing Chapel where he laid prostrate before a shrine to Caitha, mother of the forlorn, praying that his wish be granted by the goddess. This was where Gael finally encountered the Ashen One during their journey through Lothric, and managed to convince them to touch the scrap of painting, transporting them to the Painted World of Ariandel.

title: Painted World of Ariamis
snippet:
Painted World of Ariamis -  Dark Souls - location - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : The Painted World of Ariamis likely rotted and was set on fire in order to be restored. This is a usual cycle within painted worlds. The history of Painted World is no longer known in Lothric. It is taught only in the mythology of heretics, passed down just among them, and in ancient tales of hunchbacked heretics. Those heretics are Corvian Storytellers, spreading tales of Painted World among forlorn ones. They are wretched beings with no place to go, just like their followers, Corvians, the unwanted ones possessed by fear. Some of them wield Great Corvian Scythes, visually resembling the one used by the mistress of the Painted World and causing bleeding. It is a reference to Priscilla's scythe rather than Friede's, mistress of the Painted World of Ariandel.

Company Captain Yorshka is speculated to be the daughter of Crossbreed Priscilla.

title: Ariamis
snippet:
Ariamis -  Dark Souls - character - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Ariamis is the creator of the Painted World of Ariamis, a nested world that exists within a magical painting. To create this artifact the First Flame and the Dark Soul must be used as pigments, suggesting that Ariamis had access to the two primordial forces. Enclosed in a great canvas, the painted world can be accessed from the outside by touching the painting and being pulled inside by dark magic. A small fragment of the painting, even if rotten and wilted, suffices for entering a painted world. As it is within the network of bonfires, the Lordvessel allows warping inside the painting.

title: Corvian (Lore)
snippet: However, Corvian society would split when the painting began rotting, just as it had long ago. Most of the settlers wished for the painting to burn like the time before, so that a new one could be restored in its place. Friede, however, couldn't let go of the world that had become her home, convincing Ariandel to bury the flame and enlisting the Corvian Knights to protect the painting from fire. She even had her enforcer, Sir Vilhelm, hide away the Painter who was meant to see flame, just to ensure the world wouldn't be burnt to cinders.

title: The Painter
snippet: made up their minds to burn it, Friede opposed their wish, preferring a slow death in the comforting rot to the renewing change of the Flame. She convinced Ariandel to bury the flame of the Painting and to smother it using his blood, while her Corvian Knights swore to "protect" the painting from fire, even killing their own brethren who opposed her.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
If the Ashen One chooses to ignore Friede and explores the Painted World, they may fight the Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf, which allows the Ashen One to participate in the Undead Match. Deeper inside the painting, the Ashen One finds the Painter, Slave Knight Gael's aforementioned Lady, who has been imprisoned by Friede and Vilhelm in order to prevent her from painting the next world. If the Ashen One opens the way to the inner sanctum hiding Father Ariandel, Friede will confront them and fight to preserve the painting. After a long battle, the Ashen One defeats Friede and Ariandel, prompting the Painted World to begin burning and dooming it to destruction.

The Painter informs the Ashen One that she has sent Gael to find the Dark Soul, which she will use for her next painting.

title: Humans
snippet: On their quest, the Ashen One encounters the Painted World of Ariandel, and a little girl whose duty it is to become the new Painter, and replace it with a fresh, unrotted version. To do this, she reveals that she needs the blood of the bearer of the Dark Soul, and that her guardian Gael has gone to find it. At the end of time, as the flames are reduced to embers and sparks, the entire world has begun to collapse in on itself, surrounding the ageless Ringed City. Gael travels to this heap of reality to find the Dark Soul, with the Ashen One following suit, eventually slaying Argo, the leader of the Spears of the Church.

title: The Painter
snippet: The Painter was brought to the library's attic by Sir Vilhelm, who was guarding her and the key to her chamber. Vilhelm was acting on the orders of Sister Friede, who imprisoned the Painter with Father Ariandel's help. Ariandel is suppressing the Flame of the Painting with his own blood, hence only his and Friede's death can allow the Painter to see Flame. Upon being freed from house arrest, the Painter relocates from the library to the Ariandel Chapel attic. At the attic, she's found sitting in front of a big canvas; when spoken to, she divulges her vision of the new Painting. She emphasizes that the painting will show "a cold, dark, and very gentle place", which is going to be a good home for someone.

title: Ariamis
snippet: The Painted World of Ariamis was protected by an order of Painting Guardians. Anor Londo benefited from the Painted World as a prison for the spurned; it served as a place to seal away dangerous artifacts, abominations, sinners and Hollows. Velka, following from her role as the Goddess of Sin, eventually spread her influence inside the Painted World, where dozens of her cultist followers found refuge. Crossbreed Priscilla considered herself a guardian of the Painted World which she characterized as "peaceful". She pitied the "kind" inhabitants of the painting, as the outside world had shunned and locked them away, like herself. Priscilla became the "Lady" of the Painted World and its inhabitants, and welcomed the forlorn who were led into the cold world by the heretical tales of corvian storytellers. The humanoid corvians who found refuge in the Painting formed a small village, complete with knights and a library.

title: Timeline
snippet:

Over the centuries, unwanted and despised creatures are eventually drawn into the Painted World of Ariamis, where they find refuge from the outside world and legends are born about this place
Priscilla comes to consider the painting as a peaceful place and its inhabitants as kind, pledging to defend them and becoming their mistress
The order of the Painting Guardians continues to watch over Anor Londo's paintings for centuries and generations but ends up forgetting the reason for why they do it

title: Corvian Knight
snippet:
Corvian Knight -  Dark Souls III - enemy - lore 
 lore : Corvian Knights presumably protected the Corvian Settlement and its inhabitants within the Painted World of Ariandel. Whenever a Painting begins to rot, those who settled within it resolve to burn it away in order to give way for the creation of a new one. When the Corvians were faced with this event, they were prepared to burn it. However, after Sister Friede arrived in the Painting, the Corvian Knights became infatuated with her, choosing to loyally serve her and assist in her mission to let the world rot instead. To that end, the Corvian Knights betrayed their brethren, and their loyalty to Friede was so devout that they willingly slaughtered their own kin if they were perceived to be a threat.

title: Gods
snippet: The natives of the forest of Millwood worshipped an "Ethereal Oak", and the grounds of their lands from which it grew. The tree would later rot due to the dragon Midir's attempts to use it to heal himself of Abyss, and the people of Millwood moved to the Painted World of Ariandel.

title: Pyromancer's Parting Flame
snippet:
Pyromancer's Parting Flame -  Dark Souls III - weapon - availability 
 availability : Found on a corpse in the Painted World of Ariandel, in the tower where Livid Pyromancer Dunnel invades (Crossbreed Priscilla's boss arena). The path to the tower is hidden behind an illusory wall in the lower level of Ariandel Chapel basement.
